messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: [HIGH] gpu-pool-gamma memory_pressure threshold breached (node: gpu-12, usage: 96%) -- page fired to oncall-sre and infra-sre.

pagerduty: Incident 89217 triggered: gpu-pool-gamma - memory_pressure. Notify: alex (primary), priya (secondary).

alex: acked. I'm on it. pulling logs now.

priya: seeing a spike in kvcache evictions + repeated CUDA_ALLOC_FAILED in the recent logs. tagging @jamie for model-runtime angle.

jamie: on my way. do we know which model(s) are hot? any particular route?

alex: initial query: 3 user-facing routes are showing elevated latency and error rate: /v1/generate-chat (p99 up), /v1/stream (timeouts). Looks like requests are landing on pool-gamma.

alex: tailing the pod logs:
```
[2026-03-14T09:11:23Z] ERROR runtime: cuda runtime error (out of memory) : CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at kernels.cu:432
[2026-03-14T09:11:23Z] WARN kvcache: eviction triggered, evict_count=184, current_kv=14.2GB
[2026-03-14T09:11:24Z] ERROR serve: request failed: allocate failed: 0x7f38..
```

priya: node-level memory graph shows sustained GPU memory usage ~95% for last 18m. k8s OOMKiller not triggered (GPU memory not visible to host OOM), so processes are failing inside CUDA.

jamie: can we temporarily disable kvcache on this pool to free up reserved RAM? that's been the biggest consumer during long-chat sessions.

alex: planning mitigations: 1) disable kv cache on pool-gamma 2) reduce per-request max_tokens to 1024 for affected routes 3) scale up fallback CPU pool and route degraded requests 4) cordon node gpu-12 if unstable. propose we implement 1 and 2 immediately.

priya: +1. I can push a quick rollout to disable kvcache config for pool-gamma. will keep it canary to 10% first to validate.

oncall-sre: FYI, customer impact: few enterprise customers on dedicated capacity behind pool-gamma might see degraded perf or tail errors. We should surface to CS.

alex: @mike can you ping CS/AMs? we need a short blurb if this persists >30m.

mike: pinging CS now. I'll post an internal note and prepare a templated customer message.

priya: applying config: 
```
PATCH /api/v1/pools/pool-gamma/config
{ "kvcache_enabled": false, "canary_percent": 10 }
```

incident-bot: config-change: kvcache disabled canary (10%) on pool-gamma by priya.

jamie: checking kernel logs on gpu-12: seeing repeated `E CUDARuntime: driver alloc failed` entries followed by small restarts of the runtime process. Could be fragmentation + large batch sizes. Any chance a recent model rollout increased context window?

alex: yes, we rolled r2.1 of chat-model yesterday with default context 4096. Might have pushed memory use over the edge.

jamie: will roll back model r2.1 -> r2.0 on pool-gamma canary to test. initiating canary rollback to 5% traffic.

alex: issuing traffic rule to drop max_tokens and reroute CPU fallback: 
```
POST /api/v1/routing/adjust
{ "route": "/v1/stream, /v1/generate-chat", "max_tokens": 1024, "fallback_pool": "cpu-fallback", "apply_percent": 100 }
```

pagerduty: alex acknowledged incident 89217 at 2026-03-14T09:12:40Z.

eva: elevating to P1? How large is the customer impact (requests failing vs degraded)?

oncall-sre: current errors ~8% of requests on the pool, p99 latency 1.6s -> 6.5s. Error rate has been climbing over last 20m. I'd say P1 for affecting multiple tenants.

eva: OK, I'm joining. If we need to evacuate node, get green for customer notice first.

priya: canary config shows kvcache-disabled hosts are stable for last 2m, memory on those hosts dropped ~12%. will increase canary to 50% after jamie confirms.

jamie: canary rollback of r2.1 -> r2.0 at 5% shows no CUDA errors on those instances so far. seems model change was a significant contributor.

alex: increasing canary for kvcache disable to 50%.

incident-bot: config-change: kvcache disabled (canary 50%) on pool-gamma by priya.

priya: monitoring metrics: overall error rate dropping from 8% -> 3% on canary fraction. good sign. will push full disable if stable for 3m.

jamie: while this stabilizes, suggest adding a temporary request-level guard to reject requests with long context >2048 for this pool to avoid fragmentation. I can add that at the router.

alex: added a route guard: 
```
if request.context_len > 2048:
  return 413 Payload Too Large -- "context length temporarily limited"
```

mike: CS updated: "We're investigating intermittent GPU errors affecting some generation requests; teams are mitigation in progress. We'll update in 30m or sooner."

priya: full disable of kvcache on pool-gamma initiated.

incident-bot: config-change: kvcache disabled (100%) on pool-gamma by priya.

jamie: after full disable, GPU memory usage dropped across nodes by ~18% and CUDA_ALLOC_FAILED events dropped to near-zero. latency improving.

alex: great. next steps: 1) keep kvcache disabled for 24h while we analyze memory profiles 2) roll back model r2.1 where it's causing high memory; coordinate with model-owner to reduce context usage or re-quantize 3) postmortem and longer-term: improve alloc failure telemetry + auto-evacuate pattern.

eva: agreed. set an oncall follow-up: postmortem owner = jamie, timeline draft due EOD.

oncall-sre: I'm going to cordon gpu-12 as it showed the most instability and schedule a maintenance window for detailed diagnostics.

alex: cordon complete: `kubectl cordon gpu-12` -> drained non-critical pods.

incident-bot: Incident 89217 status update: mitigated - error rate back to baseline, paging suspended.

pagerduty: Incident 89217 resolved by alex at 2026-03-14T09:45:12Z (manual resolution).

jamie: quick notes for postmortem: suspicious factors: recent model r2.1 rollout, kvcache defaults that reserve large KV segments for long chats, large batch sizes. Will collect heap snapshots + nvprof traces from preserved hosts.

mike: CS draft ready for customers if we need it: "We experienced elevated errors on some generation endpoints due to GPU memory pressure. We mitigated by disabling internal KV cache and routing to fallback capacity. No customer data was exposed; we will follow up with a technical summary."

eva: please set follow-up meeting, include product, model-owner, infra-sre. Thanks everyone. :clap:

alex: thanks team. summary saved to #incidents and I'll make a short incident note in the handbook.

oncall-sre: closing thread, moving actions to jira: INF-3412 (postmortem), INF-3413 (kv cache defaults), INF-3414 (alloc telemetry).

incident-bot: Thread closed by alex.
